title: The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken
author: Nathan Lambert
summary: I feel like we’re locked in on a path of lose-lose situation, unless people embrace nuance, trade-offs, and scary realities. Much has been written about the views of various players in this debate, which I summarize as follows: Open weight models pose an untenable risk to society’s functionality , occupied by frontier lab leadership and the national security community in the U.S.
takeaways: Chinese companies continuing to release open-weight models with strong cyber capabilities , who are making decisions based on the risk assessments of their society and government.

This sort of solipsistic writing by Anthropic fits very closely to another type of discourse I’m hearing about regularly that is determining the fate of open models and AI broadly — classified briefings.

I may agree with the simple reality that closed models are far safer in the limit, as a technical tool with more layers of protection, but they may actually be causing more harm in the near term because of how accessible model APIs are.
